title: MB1-07091
frame:
Forum: Refugee Protection Division (first-instance tribunal).
Parties: the claimant and the Minister; names are redacted.
Decision under review: none; this is the first-instance decision.
How the layers nest here: The member of the tribunal is the author (layer 1). The claimant and the Minister make submissions to the member (layer 2). There is no earlier decision-maker unless the reasons describe a prior decision (layer 3). Testimony and documents are layer 5.

paragraphs.text: The following is the Panel's decision in the claims of XXXX XXXX (principal claimant), XXXX XXXX, and XXXX XXXX (minor). The claimants are seeking refugee protection pursuant to sections 96 and 97(1) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act.
At the start of the hearing, the Panel designated XXXX XXXX as the representative of her minor daughter, XXXX XXXX.
The Minister presented a Notice of Intervention concerning the principal claimant's Romanian citizenship.

The principal claimant, XXXX XXXX, is a citizen of Ukraine. He also possesses a Romanian passport. He belongs to the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. His daughter, XXXX XXXX, and grand daughter, XXXX XXXX, are citizens of Ukraine only.

The principal claimant's answer to question 31 of the Personal Information Form (PIF) describes his experience as XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, and a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. By 1999, the principal claimant, his wife and children rented a space to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX. A few years later, and without any governmental support, he and his family XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX (XXXX XXXX XXXX). The principal claimant developed strong links with XXXX XXXX and XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. He XXXX XXXX XXXX from small business owners in his area.

Around the fall of 2010, two men demanded from the principal claimant to pay 50% of the donations received from sponsors. They threatened to burn down his house and car if he did not pay. When the principal claimant explained that he did not have money, the men physically assaulted him and asked him to pay within two weeks the equivalent of US$ 6,250. Two weeks later, the extortionists visited him again, but he did not have the money. They threatened that something could happen to his granddaughter.

By 2011, the principal claimant received threatening phone calls. He decided to close the XXXX on XXXX XXXX, 2011, because he was afraid of the extortionists. His daughter, son-in-law, granddaughter and wife applied for a visa to Canada, but their application was refused. They noticed that the extortionists were following them, perhaps to verify that the XXXX was closed down. In the same year, the car of the principal claimant's son-in-law was set on fire. The principal claimant sought police protection, but the police told the family that they may have "crossed someone." The claimant complained to the police, but there was silence. Fearing for their lives, the claimant's wife, daughter, son-in-law and granddaughter unsuccessfully attempted to enter Canada illegally.

On XXXX XXXX, 2011, someone called the principal claimant to let him know that the life of his son was in danger. The next day, XXXX XXXX, 2011, someone called the principal claimant to let him know that he paid dearly for his stubbornness. The principal claimant found out that his son was brutally killed. The principal claimant asked the police to investigate the killing of his son, to give him a detailed answer on how he died, and find the murder but the prosecutors are in complete silence until today.

The principal claimant alleges that there is no state protection. Finally, the claimant's daughter secured false passports for her and her daughter, which enabled her to enter Canada. The principal claimant obtained a visitor's visa to Canada based on an American visa which he obtained to attend a XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX meeting in XXXX, Georgia.

As an annex to the answer to question 31 of the PIF, the principal claimant's wife noted that two men claiming to represent the department of human trafficking visited her house looking for XXXX, the daughter's husband. The son-in-law added at the end of the narrative that someone who alleges to be from the Department of Human Trafficking visited his family's home looking for him. Later on, two men handed him summons and took him to their office in Kiev for interrogation about a false Lithuanian passport which was in his possession. Finally, he was released.

The Minister of Public Safety submitted to the Refugee protection division (RPD) a Notice of Intervention indicating that the principal claimant declared to the Immigration Officer in Montreal that he is a citizen of Ukraine and Romania (Exhibit M-2). The Minister requested that the principal claimant be excluded under Article IE.

The panel finds the principal claimant, XXXX XXXX, and his daughter, XXXX XXXX, and the minor granddaughter, XXXX XXXX, not to be "Convention refugees". We also find, on a balance of probabilities, that the claimants would not be subjected personally to torture nor to a risk to their life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment should they return to Ukraine. The following are our reasons.

The claim is based on the issue of state protection. The Principal claimant's answer to question 31 of the PIF starts with his background as XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in Ukraine. He submitted XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX in support of this background. He also provided documents related to his affiliation with the XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. The panel will not address these documents as they do not relate to the thrust of the claim.
We believe the Ukrainian authorities have genuinely attempted to investigate the claimants' grievances, but the claimants do not accept the findings.

The Principal claimant and his daughter, XXXX XXXX, testified that the daughter's car was set on fire by criminal elements. In support of this claim, the claimants submitted exhibits D-10 to D-16. We believe these exhibits demonstrate that the authorities have conducted an investigation of the car burning, but were unable to identify the culprits. Among the exhibits, we note summons that were issued to XXXX XXXX and her husband to provide evidence concerning the burning of the car. A fire report was prepared by the Fire Department and attributed the cause to arson. A final investigation report was issued, and the police decided not to open a criminal investigation.

Based on exhibits D-10 to D-16, we believe the authorities acted in good faith and did all they could under the circumstances to investigate the burning of the car. However, the findings were not to the satisfaction to the claimants.

The claimants submitted exhibits D-6 to D-9 in support of the claim that the extortionists killed his son, XXXX. The principal claimant also submitted photos of the deceased son, showing a naked body with serious injuries.

Additional exhibits which were submitted by the principal claimant show that the authorities have investigated the son's death. Exhibit D-8 is a document dated XXXX XXXX XXXX 2011, issued by the Acting Junior Justice Councillor in the Ukraine's Prosecutor's Office and addressed to the Deputy Head of Administration in the State Prosecutor's Office, with a copy to the principal claimant. The document informs the Deputy Head of the principal claimant's concern about the "inadequate" pre-trial investigation in the son's death. Exhibit D-9, issued on XXXX XXXX, 2011 by the Acting Head of Administration of the Oblast Public Prosecution Office, informs the Head of the Investigation Department in the Ministry of Interior of the principal claimant's concerns about the inadequate pre-trial investigation and requests the results of the investigation.

When asked if he has any additional documents to shed light on the outcome of the investigation, the principal claimant noted that the prosecutors are in "complete silence till today" and that the prosecutor's office did not follow up on the investigation.

We do not believe the principal claimant's allegation that the state has not acted on his complaint and that there is "complete silence till today." Exhibit D-9 (the principal claimant's complaint about the inadequate investigation) makes reference to 7 additional pages which are the principal claimant's complaint to the prosecutor's office about the inadequacy of the investigation. These 7 pages were not included in the documents which the principal claimant submitted to the panel. When asked for these pages, the principal claimant mentioned that there is complete police silence.

Moreover, the principal claimant submitted exhibit D-9 (Letter of State Prosecutor, XXXX XXXX XXXX 2012), which makes reference to Section 286 (2) of the Criminal Code of Ukraine. This section of the Criminal Code of Ukraine addresses drivers' violation of rules related to traffic or driving safety: 1. Violation of rules related to traffic or driving safety by a person that drives any vehicle, where it caused medium grave bodily injury to the punishable by a fine of 200 to 500 tax-free minimum incomes, or correctional labor for victim, -shall be a term up to two years, or arrest for a term up to six months, or restraint of liberty for a term up to three years, with or without the deprivation of the right to operate transport for a term up to three years. 2. The same acts that caused death or grave bodily injury of the victim, - shall be punishable by imprisonment for a term of three to eight years with or without the deprivation of the right to operate transport for a term up to three years. 3. Any such acts as provided for by paragraph 1 of this Article, if they caused death of several persons, - shall be punishable by imprisonment for a term of five to ten years with the deprivation of the right to operate transport for a term up to three years. Note: For the purposes of the present Article and Articles 287, 289 and 290, vehicles shall mean all types of cars, tractors and other self-propelled machines, trams, trolley buses, motor cycles, and other vehicles.(Article 286 as amended by Laws No 270-VI (270-17) of 15.04.2008, No 586-VI (586-17) of 24.09.2008).

We believe that the claimant's son was killed in a road accident, and that the state has acted on the principal claimant's complaint. Evidence shows that the prosecutor pursued the principal claimant's complaint about the inadequacy of the investigation, convened the claimant's daughter to investigate the complaint, and reported the complaint to his superiors. Although the claimants are unhappy with the findings of the investigation, they did not show, on a balance of probabilities, that state protection is inadequate. The panel has serious doubts about the cause of the son's death.

The principal claimant submitted exhibit D-17 to indicate that he, his wife and daughter have received psychological help. The psychologist diagnosed the principal claimant with moderate to severe depression and anxiety. The report attributed the depression and anxiety to "events in his professional life"-long-term stress, threats to his life and murder of his son.
We do not question the son's death; however, exhibit D-9 makes reference to a road accident.
As the panel found that there is adequate state protection in Ukraine, the panel did not address the Minister's Intervention regarding the principal claimant's Romanian citizenship.
Based on the above analysis, the panel concludes that the claimants are not "Convention refugees" and are not "persons in need of protection."

Consequently, the claims for refugee protection for XXXX XXXX, XXXX XXXX, and XXXX XXXXXXXX (minor) are rejected. Ayman Yassini Ayman Yassini December 3, 2012 /ajh Date RPD File No. / No dossier SPR : MB1-07091 MB1-07094 MB1-07101 6
